home.title: Tutorials
home.text: Go back over where to start, or discover a module in a few steps.

novel.title: Starting a novel
novel.name: Novel
novel.intro: From the first idea to the exported manuscript, with the Manuscript module, reserved for novels.

start.title: Lay out your story
start.text: Start with a few lines: what is this novel about? The synopsis can later be the base of your editorial file.
points: Details › Project synopsis: summary, genres, subgenres and tone.
Nothing is set in stone: come back to it as often as you need.

plan.title: Build the outline
plan.text: A novel is split into parts, chapters and scenes. The outline decides the order of the manuscript.
points: Structure › Story outline: add your parts, chapters and scenes.
No need for parts: a chapter can sit directly at the root of the outline.
Moving a scene in the outline also moves it in the manuscript.

write.title: Write in the sheets
write.text: The text is written in the sheet of a scene, or of a chapter without scenes: the “Text” card. The “Writing” card keeps your goal and narration choices.
points: Open a scene from the outline, then write in the “Text” card.
“Writing”: word goal, writing state, point of view, person and tense.
The text is saved with the sheet (Ctrl+S or autosave) and keeps its versions.

import.title: Already have a text?
import.text: Import a Word, Markdown or text file: GANIS splits it into parts, chapters and scenes.
points: Manuscript › Import a manuscript.
Without an import, a scene can also use the text of a document filed on it.

manuscript.title: Read and export the manuscript
manuscript.text: The manuscript assembles the whole novel in one piece, in outline order. Nothing is copied: it is always up to date.
points: Manuscript › Manuscript, or the ▶ button in the title bar (F5) to read in the whole space.
Export to Word, PDF or text, with a title page and chapters starting on a new page.

progress.title: Track your writing
progress.text: Tracking gathers words and goals, from the whole novel down to the scene, and flags narration changes.
points: Filter chapters by state: to write, first draft, in revision, proofread, corrected.
A scene whose person or tense differs from the rest of the novel is flagged.
Set a daily goal and follow your session and your streak.

replace.title: Correct across the whole novel
replace.text: A character changes name? Find and replace corrects a name or a word across all the scene text.
points: Manuscript › Find and replace.

editorial.title: Prepare the editorial file
editorial.text: The texts that present the novel to a publisher or an agent, independent from the synopsis.
points: One-sentence pitch, short summary and long summary.
“Start from the synopsis” gives you a first base.
Each text is exported separately.

manga.title: Starting a manga
manga.name: Manga
manga.intro: From the volume to the panel, up to reading the whole story, with the Script module, reserved for manga and comics.

start.title: Lay out your story
start.text: Start with a few lines: what is this series about, and in what tone?
points: Details › Project synopsis: summary, genres, subgenres and tone.
Create your characters and locations whenever you like: panels can refer to them.

plan.title: Build the outline
plan.text: A manga is split into volumes, chapters and pages. The outline decides the reading order.
points: Structure › Story outline: add a volume, then its chapters.
For a comic or a one-shot, keep only the levels you need.

chapter.title: Prepare a chapter
chapter.text: A chapter's sheet has its “Chapter script” card: what it must achieve, how many pages it aims for, and where it stands.
points: Narrative goal, target pages and status.
“Add pages” creates several pages in one go.

panels.title: Write the page, panel by panel
panels.text: A page's “Panels” card describes what the reader sees: action, framing, characters and texts.
points: Texts: dialogue, thought, narration, sound effect, scenery text.
Give a character a state (injury, outfit…): the Continuity view picks it up.
“Page turn”: plans a reveal for the next page.
A page or panel with too much text is flagged.
Without art, the sheet shows a page template based on the number of panels: “Other layout” offers more.

art.title: File the art
art.text: Drop each piece of art on its page's sheet: it shows next to its panels.
points: “Documents” card: “Add files”, or drag and drop.
A chapter's “Read the pages” chains its art.
Art filed on the chapter is shared out over its pages, in order.

read.title: Read and export the story
read.text: The story chapter by chapter: what each chapter is about, then what its pages show.
points: The table of contents, on the left, leads to a chapter; the pencil opens its sheet.
“Export” saves the story as Word, PDF or text.
The ▶ button in the title bar (F5) starts reading in the whole space.

flatplan.title: Check the flatplan
flatplan.text: All of a volume's pages as spreads, in the chosen reading direction: empty, script written or art filed.
points: Right to left for a manga, left to right for a comic.
The number of the first page decides which pages face each other.
A reveal badly placed relative to the page turn is flagged.

progress.title: Track progress
progress.text: Planned and written pages, statuses and text volume, chapter by chapter.
points: Set the alert thresholds: words per panel and words per page.
These alerts are only indicative: readability also depends on balloons and art.

continuity.title: Keep continuity
continuity.text: Pick a character: every panel they appear in, with their state, location and moment.
points: See at a glance where their state changes.
Filter by location to check a specific scene.

story.title: Starting a project: {{type}}
story.name: {{type}}
story.intro: The main steps to build your story, from the idea to the full read.

start.title: Lay out your story
start.text: Start with a few lines: what is this project about, and in what tone?
points: Details › Project synopsis: summary, genres, subgenres and tone.

cast.title: Create your characters
cast.text: One sheet per character, from the simplest to the most detailed, then their relationships.
points: Characters › Create a character, or Ctrl+N in the module.
The relationship graph shows who is linked to whom.

world.title: Build your world
world.text: From the continent to the room: locations fit inside one another.
points: Need objects, animals or plants? Turn on those modules in the project settings.

plan.title: Split up the story
plan.text: For this type of project, the outline offers by default: {{levels}}. You can rename these levels in the settings.
points: Structure › Story outline: add the items and arrange them.
Each item has its sheet: summary, text, characters, locations and documents.

plot.title: Weave the plots
plot.text: The board shows your plots in columns, time running downward, and their cause-and-effect links.
points: Double-click in a column to place an event.
Attach an event to an outline item: it feeds the full read.

read.title: Read the whole story
read.text: The full read compiles the story in outline order: summaries, texts and documents, or otherwise the plot's events.
points: The ▶ button in the title bar (F5) shows it in the whole space.
It can be exported to Word, PDF or text.

characters.title: Tutorial: Characters
characters.name: Characters
characters.intro: Your characters' sheets and what links them.

create.title: Create a character
create.text: Identity, appearance and personality: fill in only what is useful to you.
points: Each sheet opens in its own tab.
Ctrl+N in the module creates a character.

level.title: Choose the level of detail
level.text: Essential, intermediate or advanced: this level applies to all the project's sheets.
points: Fields already filled in are never erased when you change it.

images.title: Add images
images.text: A main image, a reference gallery and a color palette on each sheet.
points: Drag your images straight onto the sheet.
The palette's colors frame the portrait.

relations.title: Link them
relations.text: Family, friendships, rivalries, alliances: the graph shows everyone at a glance.
points: Characters move freely in the graph.
From the sheet, also link a character to their locations.

locations.title: Tutorial: Locations
locations.name: Locations
locations.intro: Your story's geography, from the continent to the room.

create.title: Create a location
create.text: The type of a location (city, forest, palace…) chooses the fields on its sheet.
points: Each sheet has a banner, a gallery and a color palette.

nest.title: Fit locations inside one another
nest.text: A continent contains kingdoms, which contain cities. The panel shows them as a tree.
points: “Add a place in…” creates a location inside another.

types.title: Add your own types
types.text: A particular universe? The project settings take your own location types and statuses.

links.title: Link them to the story
links.text: Characters linked to a location appear on its sheet, and structure items show their locations.
points: Where a character lives, works, grew up — with the story period if needed.

items.title: Tutorial: Objects
items.name: Objects
items.intro: Weapons, vehicles, phones, magical objects… everything that matters in your story.

enable.title: Turn on the module
enable.text: The Objects module is optional: it appears in the left bar only once turned on in the project settings.
points: Turning it off later deletes nothing: your sheets are kept.

categories.title: Keep the useful categories
categories.text: Choose what your story needs: only these categories are offered when creating.
points: Add your own types and statuses.
Set the level of detail of the module's sheets.

create.title: Create an object
create.text: Choose its type: the sheet adapts to a weapon, a vehicle, a phone…
points: Add an image, a gallery and a color palette.
Ctrl+N in the module creates an object.

nest.title: Arrange the objects
nest.text: An object can be placed inside another, like a key in a chest. The panel shows them as a tree.

links.title: Link them to the story
links.text: On the sheet, link an object to a character, a location or another object: “owns”, “is part of”…
points: Give a story period when an object changes hands.

species.title: Tutorial: Fauna and flora
species.name: Fauna and flora
species.intro: The animals and plants of your universe, from a whole species to the individual with a name.

enable.title: Turn on the module
enable.text: Fauna and flora is optional: it appears in the left bar only once turned on in the project settings.
points: Then choose the useful categories and the level of detail.
Turning it off later deletes nothing.

nature.title: Species or individual?
nature.text: A sheet describes either a whole species (grey wolves, the moon rose), or a specific animal or plant (Lightning, the hero's horse).
points: Choose its nature when creating it: the sheet's fields adapt.

hierarchy.title: File individuals under their species
hierarchy.text: The panel shows species as a tree, with their individuals.

character.title: An animal can be a character
character.text: Your animal talks or has relationships? On its sheet, create its character sheet, or associate it with an existing character.
points: The two sheets stay linked.

links.title: Link them to the story
links.text: On the sheet, link them to characters, locations, objects and other species: “lives in”, “belongs to”…
points: Give a story period if needed.

structure.title: Tutorial: Structure
structure.name: Structure
structure.intro: The outline of your story. For this project, by default: {{levels}}.

plan.title: Build the outline
plan.text: Add your items in Story outline: they form a tree, numbered for you.
points: Take an item out of the numbering for a prologue or an interlude.

sheet.title: Fill in the sheets
sheet.text: Each item has its sheet: summary, characters (point of view, present…) and locations.
points: The Plot module can also attach to it.

documents.title: File the documents
documents.text: PDF, Word, images, sounds: file them on an item's sheet, with “Add files” or by drag and drop.
points: Click a document to read it in GANIS.
“Edit in its application” picks up every save and keeps older versions.

settings.title: Adapt the levels
settings.text: In the project settings: the name of each level, automatic numbering and colors.

plot.title: Tutorial: Plot
plot.name: Plot
plot.intro: Your parallel plots on a single board: one column per plot, time running downward.

board.title: Place the events
board.text: Double-click in a column to place an event; drag the cards to change their moment or plot.
points: Go above moment 1 for the narrative past: flashbacks and memories.
Ctrl+Z undoes each gesture on the board.

links.title: Link them
links.text: Pull a card's round handle toward another: impact, influence or crossing.
points: The “Tension” button shows the tension curve.

connect.title: Attach them to the project
connect.text: Point of view, characters present, location, outline chapter and notes: everything links from the event.
points: Linked sheets show these events under “In the plot”.

reading.title: Read in the reader's order
reading.text: Story reading shows the events in reading order, by default that of the outline.
points: “Walk through” follows the story event by event, right on the board.

notes.title: Tutorial: Notes
notes.name: Notes
notes.intro: Everything that fits nowhere else: research, ideas, documentation.

create.title: Create a note
create.text: A note is written with a real editor, saved and versioned like the rest of the project.

editor.title: Structure your ideas
editor.text: Headings, lists, tables and links, but also callouts, linked boxes and diagrams.
points: Less common tools are in the “…” menu at the end of the bar.

organize.title: Arrange your notes
organize.text: Sort notes into folders by drag and drop, and pin the most important ones.

wall.title: Empty your head on the wall
wall.text: The sticky-note wall takes ideas in bulk: move them by their strip, resize them by their corner.
